model.chicago_311.int_service_requests.name: int_service_requests
model.chicago_311.int_service_requests.description: Request-level fact table. One row per sr_number after deduplication, with status and department normalised, closure duration computed, and one boolean per data-quality defect so the defects can be counted anywhere downstream. Incremental on last_modified_at, see the comment at the top of the model for why.

sr_number.name: sr_number
sr_number.description: City-assigned request id. Unique in this model, which is the point of the dedup step.

service_type.name: service_type
service_type.description: Long request type name, unchanged from source.

service_type_key.name: service_type_key
service_type_key.description: Uppercased punctuation-free form of service_type, produced by the normalize_label macro.

service_code.name: service_code
service_code.description: Short internal code for the request type.

department.name: department
department.description: Owning department with the acronym prefix stripped, for example "Department of Transportation".

status.name: status
status.description: Normalised lifecycle status. "Completed" absorbs the raw "Closed" spelling.

status_raw.name: status_raw
status_raw.description: Status exactly as published, kept so the normalisation can be audited.

ward.name: ward
ward.description: Cleaned ward number. NULL when the source ward was blank or outside 1-50.

police_district.name: police_district
police_district.description: Police district of the service address.

zip_code.name: zip_code
zip_code.description: Five digit ZIP of the service address.

created_month.name: created_month
created_month.description: created_at truncated to the first of the month. Grain for all time series in the marts.

created_year.name: created_year
created_year.description: Calendar year the request was opened. Either 2023 or 2024 by construction.

created_day_of_week.name: created_day_of_week
created_day_of_week.description: Day of week of created_at, 0 = Sunday.

last_modified_at.name: last_modified_at
last_modified_at.description: Last time the City touched the record. Drives the incremental filter.

closed_at.name: closed_at
closed_at.description: Timestamp the request was closed, NULL if never closed.

days_to_close_raw.name: days_to_close_raw
days_to_close_raw.description: Signed days between created_at and closed_at. Can be negative, which is a real defect. Present only so the defect is auditable, never used in a mart.

days_to_close.name: days_to_close
days_to_close.description: Analysis-ready closure duration in days. Populated only when the request is Completed and closed_at is not earlier than created_at. This is the column every mart measures.

days_open.name: days_open
days_open.description: Age in days of a still-open request as of the window end date. NULL for anything not Open.

is_stale_open.name: is_stale_open
is_stale_open.description: True for requests still Open more than stale_open_days after creation. NULL for anything not Open.

has_backwards_timestamps.name: has_backwards_timestamps
has_backwards_timestamps.description: True when closed_at is earlier than created_at. Defect 4.

is_closed_without_timestamp.name: is_closed_without_timestamp
is_closed_without_timestamp.description: True when status is Completed but closed_at is NULL. Defect 7.

has_unknown_ward.name: has_unknown_ward
has_unknown_ward.description: True when the ward could not be resolved to 1-50. Defect 3.

has_no_geocode.name: has_no_geocode
has_no_geocode.description: True when latitude or longitude is missing. Defect 8.

is_legacy_record.name: is_legacy_record
is_legacy_record.description: True for records migrated from the pre-2018 system.

parent_sr_number.name: parent_sr_number
parent_sr_number.description: Surviving request id when this request was merged into another.

source_file.name: source_file
source_file.description: Raw CSV page this row came from.

model.chicago_311.int_service_requests.raw_code:
{{
    config(
        materialized = 'incremental',
        unique_key = 'sr_number',
        incremental_strategy = 'delete+insert'
    )
}}

{#
    Why incremental is the right choice here and not anywhere else in this project
    --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    This is the only model in the project that is both large and append-mostly.
    It carries roughly 690k rows of per-request enrichment over a two-year
    window, and 311 records behave the same way in production as they do here:
    a request is created once, gets touched a few times while it is open, and
    then never changes again. Over 95% of the rows in this table are closed
    requests whose last_modified_date is months in the past. Recomputing them on
    every run is work with a known-zero result.

    The incremental filter is on last_modified_at, not created_at. Filtering on
    created_at would be wrong: a pothole opened in March and closed in
    September would be frozen at its March state forever, and the whole point
    of the project is closure duration. last_modified_at moves whenever the
    City touches the record, so it catches late closures of old requests.

    delete+insert rather than append, because a re-pulled month legitimately
    contains updated copies of rows already in the table, and append would turn
    every one of those into a duplicate. unique_key is sr_number, so an updated
    request replaces its old row.

    The marts downstream are deliberately NOT incremental. They are aggregates
    in the low thousands of rows and rebuild in under a second, so incremental
    logic there would add failure modes and save nothing.
#}

with base as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_service_requests') }}

    {% if is_incremental() %}
        -- Only rows the City has touched since the last build, with a one-day
        -- overlap because last_modified_date is published at day granularity
        -- for some records and a strict > would skip same-timestamp updates.
        where last_modified_at >= (
            select coalesce(max(last_modified_at), '1900-01-01'::timestamp) - interval 1 day
            from {{ this }}
        )
    {% endif %}

),

deduplicated as (

    -- Defect 1 in docs/DATA_QUALITY.md: sr_number is not unique in the raw
    -- feed. Keep the most recently modified copy of each request, because that
    -- is the City's current view of it. Ties broken by closed_at so the result
    -- is deterministic rather than dependent on scan order.
    select *
    from base
    qualify row_number() over (
        partition by sr_number
        order by last_modified_at desc nulls last,
                 closed_at desc nulls last
    ) = 1

),

normalised as (

    select
        sr_number,
        sr_type                                     as service_type,
        sr_short_code                               as service_code,
        {{ normalize_label('sr_type') }}            as service_type_key,

        -- Department names in the raw feed are a mix of "Streets and
        -- Sanitation" and "DWM - Department of Water Management". Strip the
        -- acronym prefix so a dashboard legend reads consistently.
        case
            when owner_department like '% - %'
                then trim(split_part(owner_department, ' - ', 2))
            else owner_department
        end                                         as department,

        -- Defect 5: "Completed" (the overwhelming majority) and "Closed" (a
        -- single row) are the same state. Collapse them.
        case
            when {{ normalize_label('status_raw') }} in ('COMPLETED', 'CLOSED') then 'Completed'
            when {{ normalize_label('status_raw') }} = 'CANCELED' then 'Canceled'
            when {{ normalize_label('status_raw') }} = 'OPEN' then 'Open'
            else 'Unknown'
        end                                         as status,
        status_raw,

        origin,
        ward,
        ward_raw,
        community_area,
        police_district,
        zip_code,
        latitude,
        longitude,

        created_at,
        last_modified_at,
        closed_at,
        is_flagged_duplicate,
        is_legacy_record,
        parent_sr_number,
        source_file

    from deduplicated

),

enriched as (

    select
        *,

        cast(created_at as date)                            as created_date,
        date_trunc('month', created_at)                     as created_month,
        extract(year from created_at)                       as created_year,
        extract(dow from created_at)                        as created_day_of_week,

        status = 'Completed'                                as is_closed,
        status = 'Open'                                     as is_open,
        status = 'Canceled'                                 as is_canceled,

        -- Raw duration, signed. Negative values are kept here so that the
        -- defect stays visible and the singular tests can see it.
        case
            when closed_at is not null
                then {{ duration_days('created_at', 'closed_at') }}
        end                                                 as days_to_close_raw,

        -- Analysis-ready duration. NULL unless the request is genuinely closed
        -- with a closed_at that is not before its created_at. Every mart uses
        -- this column, which is why the negative rows cannot leak into a median.
        case
            when status = 'Completed'
                 and closed_at is not null
                 and closed_at >= created_at
                then {{ duration_days('created_at', 'closed_at') }}
        end                                                 as days_to_close,

        -- Age of a still-open request as of the end of the analysis window.
        -- A fixed reference date rather than current_date, so the numbers in
        -- the README do not drift every time someone re-runs the project.
        case
            when status = 'Open'
                then {{ duration_days('created_at', "'" ~ var('window_end') ~ "'::timestamp") }}
        end                                                 as days_open,

        -- Defect 6: requests sitting open for more than a year are backlog, not
        -- live work, and a department head would want them separated out.
        case
            when status = 'Open'
                 and {{ duration_days('created_at', "'" ~ var('window_end') ~ "'::timestamp") }} > {{ var('stale_open_days') }}
                then true
            when status = 'Open' then false
        end                                                 as is_stale_open,

        -- Defect 4: closure recorded before creation. Impossible, flagged.
        coalesce(closed_at < created_at, false)             as has_backwards_timestamps,

        -- Defect 7: the City calls it completed but gave no closure timestamp.
        (status = 'Completed' and closed_at is null)        as is_closed_without_timestamp,

        ward is null                                        as has_unknown_ward,
        (latitude is null or longitude is null)             as has_no_geocode

    from normalised

)

select * from enriched
where created_at >= '{{ var("window_start") }}'::timestamp
  and created_at <  '{{ var("window_end") }}'::timestamp

model.chicago_311.int_ward_monthly_load.name: int_ward_monthly_load
model.chicago_311.int_ward_monthly_load.description: Ward by month workload and closure-speed panel, 50 wards x 24 months. This is the table the volume hypothesis is tested on.

created_month.name: created_month
created_month.description: Month the requests were opened in.

requests_opened.name: requests_opened
requests_opened.description: Count of requests opened in the ward that month.

requests_closed_cleanly.name: requests_closed_cleanly
requests_closed_cleanly.description: Of those, how many have a usable closure duration.

median_days_to_close.name: median_days_to_close
median_days_to_close.description: Median days_to_close for requests opened that month. NULL if none closed cleanly.

mean_days_to_close.name: mean_days_to_close
mean_days_to_close.description: Mean days_to_close for requests opened that month.

p90_days_to_close.name: p90_days_to_close
p90_days_to_close.description: 90th percentile closure time, which is what a resident in the tail actually experiences.

still_open.name: still_open
still_open.description: Count of requests from that month still Open.

ward_avg_monthly_requests.name: ward_avg_monthly_requests
ward_avg_monthly_requests.description: The ward's own mean monthly request count across the window.

load_index.name: load_index
load_index.description: requests_opened divided by the ward's own average month. 1.0 is a typical month for that ward, 1.5 is a 50% heavier month. Normalising within ward is what separates a load spike from a ward simply being big.

model.chicago_311.int_ward_monthly_load.raw_code:
-- Workload a ward handed the City in each month, and the median closure time
-- for the requests opened in that month. This is the grain the volume
-- hypothesis gets tested at: if backlog drives delay, then months where a ward
-- files unusually many requests should be the months its closure times get
-- worse. Keeping it monthly rather than annual gives 50 wards x 24 months =
-- 1200 observations instead of 100, which is what makes the correlation in
-- mart_volume_vs_delay worth reporting.

with requests as (

    select *
    from {{ ref('int_service_requests') }}
    where ward is not null

),

by_ward_month as (

    select
        ward,
        created_month,
        count(*)                                            as requests_opened,
        count(days_to_close)                                as requests_closed_cleanly,
        median(days_to_close)                               as median_days_to_close,
        avg(days_to_close)                                   as mean_days_to_close,
        quantile_cont(days_to_close, 0.90)                   as p90_days_to_close,
        sum(case when is_open then 1 else 0 end)             as still_open

    from requests
    group by ward, created_month

)

select
    bwm.*,
    w.ward_name,
    w.city_side,

    -- Each ward's own typical month, so a month can be described as heavy or
    -- light relative to that ward rather than relative to the city. Ward 42
    -- always outvolumes ward 19; that is a size difference, not a load spike.
    avg(bwm.requests_opened) over (partition by bwm.ward)   as ward_avg_monthly_requests,
    bwm.requests_opened
        / nullif(avg(bwm.requests_opened) over (partition by bwm.ward), 0) as load_index

from by_ward_month bwm
join {{ ref('stg_wards') }} w on w.ward = bwm.ward

model.chicago_311.mart_monthly_trend.name: mart_monthly_trend
model.chicago_311.mart_monthly_trend.description: Service type by month, with year-over-year comparison. Carries the seasonality result, which is where the pothole wait actually comes from.

created_month.name: created_month
created_month.description: First of the month the requests were opened in.

month_of_year.name: month_of_year
month_of_year.description: 1-12, so the two years can be overlaid on one axis.

requests_opened.name: requests_opened
requests_opened.description: Requests of this type opened citywide that month.

requests_measurable.name: requests_measurable
requests_measurable.description: Of those, how many have a usable closure duration.

requests_still_open.name: requests_still_open
requests_still_open.description: Of those, how many are still Open.

median_days_to_close.name: median_days_to_close
median_days_to_close.description: Median wait for requests opened that month.

p90_days_to_close.name: p90_days_to_close
p90_days_to_close.description: 90th percentile wait for requests opened that month.

share_closed_within_7d.name: share_closed_within_7d
share_closed_within_7d.description: Fraction closed inside a week, 0 to 1.

median_days_to_close_ly.name: median_days_to_close_ly
median_days_to_close_ly.description: The same month one year earlier. NULL for all of 2023.

median_days_change_yoy.name: median_days_change_yoy
median_days_change_yoy.description: median_days_to_close minus median_days_to_close_ly. Positive means the wait got worse.

volume_index.name: volume_index
volume_index.description: That month's volume over the service type's average month. 1.0 is typical.

model.chicago_311.mart_monthly_trend.raw_code:
-- Monthly volume and wait by service type, with the city side split out.
-- This mart exists because of what the pothole numbers turned out to look
-- like: volume peaks in February and the wait is shortest in February, and the
-- wait is worst in May when volume has already halved. That pattern is only
-- visible at a monthly grain, so it needs its own table rather than being
-- derived from the ward mart.

with requests as (

    select * from {{ ref('int_service_requests') }}

),

monthly as (

    select
        created_month,
        created_year,
        extract(month from created_month)                   as month_of_year,
        service_type,
        department,

        count(*)                                            as requests_opened,
        count(days_to_close)                                as requests_measurable,
        sum(case when is_open then 1 else 0 end)            as requests_still_open,

        median(days_to_close)                                as median_days_to_close,
        quantile_cont(days_to_close, 0.90)                   as p90_days_to_close,
        sum(case when days_to_close <= 7 then 1 else 0 end)
            / nullif(count(days_to_close), 0)::double        as share_closed_within_7d

    from requests
    group by created_month, created_year, service_type, department

)

select
    m.*,

    -- Same month a year earlier, so year-over-year change is in the table.
    -- The 2024 pothole off-season was far worse than 2023 and that comparison
    -- is the single most useful number in this mart.
    lag(m.median_days_to_close, 12) over (
        partition by m.service_type order by m.created_month
    )                                                       as median_days_to_close_ly,

    m.median_days_to_close - lag(m.median_days_to_close, 12) over (
        partition by m.service_type order by m.created_month
    )                                                       as median_days_change_yoy,

    m.requests_opened / nullif(
        avg(m.requests_opened) over (partition by m.service_type), 0
    )                                                       as volume_index

from monthly m

model.chicago_311.mart_ward_service_perf.name: mart_ward_service_performance
model.chicago_311.mart_ward_service_perf.description: One row per ward x service type. Volume next to wait time, which is the pairing the business question needs. Drives dashboard views 1 and 2.

requests_total.name: requests_total
requests_total.description: All requests of this type in this ward over the two-year window.

requests_measurable.name: requests_measurable
requests_measurable.description: Subset with a usable closure duration. Denominator for every rate on this row.

requests_open.name: requests_open
requests_open.description: Count still Open at the end of the window.

requests_canceled.name: requests_canceled
requests_canceled.description: Count the City canceled rather than completed.

requests_duplicate.name: requests_duplicate
requests_duplicate.description: Count the City flagged as duplicates of another request.

median_days_to_close.name: median_days_to_close
median_days_to_close.description: Median days from open to close. The headline wait-time measure.

mean_days_to_close.name: mean_days_to_close
mean_days_to_close.description: Mean days to close. Reported alongside the median because the gap between them is the tail.

p90_days_to_close.name: p90_days_to_close
p90_days_to_close.description: 90th percentile wait. What the unlucky tenth of residents experience.

share_closed_within_7d.name: share_closed_within_7d
share_closed_within_7d.description: Fraction of measurable requests closed inside a week, 0 to 1.

share_closed_under_1min.name: share_closed_under_1min
share_closed_under_1min.description: Fraction closed in under 60 seconds. A data-quality signal, not a performance one. Graffiti runs high here, see DATA_QUALITY defect 2.

slowest_rank_in_service.name: slowest_rank_in_service
slowest_rank_in_service.description: 1 means this ward is the slowest in the city for this service type.

volume_rank_in_service.name: volume_rank_in_service
volume_rank_in_service.description: 1 means this ward files the most of this service type.

median_vs_city_ratio.name: median_vs_city_ratio
median_vs_city_ratio.description: This ward's median divided by the typical ward median for the same service. Above 1 is slower than typical.

model.chicago_311.mart_ward_service_perf.raw_code:
-- Core answer table: how long each ward waits for each service type, next to
-- how much of that service the ward asks for. One row per ward x service type.
-- Everything in the dashboard's first two views reads off this.

with requests as (

    select * from {{ ref('int_service_requests') }}
    where ward is not null

),

agg as (

    select
        ward,
        service_type,
        department,

        count(*)                                        as requests_total,
        count(days_to_close)                            as requests_measurable,
        sum(case when is_open then 1 else 0 end)        as requests_open,
        sum(case when is_canceled then 1 else 0 end)    as requests_canceled,
        sum(case when is_flagged_duplicate then 1 else 0 end) as requests_duplicate,

        median(days_to_close)                           as median_days_to_close,
        avg(days_to_close)                              as mean_days_to_close,
        quantile_cont(days_to_close, 0.90)              as p90_days_to_close,

        -- Share closed inside a week. A median hides the tail, and the tail is
        -- what generates the alderman phone call.
        sum(case when days_to_close <= 7 then 1 else 0 end)
            / nullif(count(days_to_close), 0)::double   as share_closed_within_7d,

        -- Share closed in under a minute. Not a performance number, a data
        -- quality number: see docs/DATA_QUALITY.md defect 2. Surfaced in the
        -- mart so nobody reads a 0.7 day graffiti median as a real wait.
        sum(case when days_to_close < 1.0/1440 then 1 else 0 end)
            / nullif(count(days_to_close), 0)::double   as share_closed_under_1min

    from requests
    group by ward, service_type, department

)

select
    a.ward,
    w.ward_name,
    w.city_side,
    a.service_type,
    a.department,
    a.requests_total,
    a.requests_measurable,
    a.requests_open,
    a.requests_canceled,
    a.requests_duplicate,
    a.median_days_to_close,
    a.mean_days_to_close,
    a.p90_days_to_close,
    a.share_closed_within_7d,
    a.share_closed_under_1min,

    -- Rank within the service type, so "ward 36 is slowest for potholes" is a
    -- number in the table rather than something the dashboard has to derive.
    row_number() over (
        partition by a.service_type order by a.median_days_to_close desc nulls last
    )                                                   as slowest_rank_in_service,
    row_number() over (
        partition by a.service_type order by a.requests_total desc
    )                                                   as volume_rank_in_service,

    -- How this ward compares to the city on the same service. Above 1 means
    -- slower than the typical ward for that service.
    a.median_days_to_close / nullif(
        median(a.median_days_to_close) over (partition by a.service_type), 0
    )                                                   as median_vs_city_ratio

from agg a
join {{ ref('stg_wards') }} w on w.ward = a.ward

model.chicago_311.stg_service_requests.name: stg_service_requests
model.chicago_311.stg_service_requests.description: One row per raw 311 request record, renamed and typed. Lossless by design: no rows are dropped and no values are repaired here, so this model is the right place to measure data quality from. Duplicate sr_numbers are still present at this stage.

sr_number.name: sr_number
sr_number.description: City-assigned service request id. Not unique at this stage, see docs/DATA_QUALITY.md defect 1.

sr_type.name: sr_type
sr_type.description: Long service-request type name, for example "Pothole in Street Complaint".

sr_short_code.name: sr_short_code
sr_short_code.description: Three or four character internal code for the request type, for example GRAF.

owner_department.name: owner_department
owner_department.description: Department that owns the work. Naming is inconsistent in the raw feed (some entries are prefixed with an acronym, some are not), so the marts use the normalised version from int_service_requests.

status_raw.name: status_raw
status_raw.description: Lifecycle status exactly as published. Renamed with a _raw suffix because it needs normalising: "Completed" and "Closed" mean the same thing and both appear.

origin.name: origin
origin.description: Intake channel, for example Phone Call, Mobile Device, Internet.

created_at.name: created_at
created_at.description: Timestamp the request was opened. Cast with try_cast so an unparseable value becomes NULL instead of failing the run.

last_modified_at.name: last_modified_at
last_modified_at.description: Timestamp of the last update of any kind to the record. Drives the incremental filter in int_service_requests.

closed_at.name: closed_at
closed_at.description: Timestamp the request was closed. NULL for open requests, and also NULL for some records the City reports as completed.

is_flagged_duplicate.name: is_flagged_duplicate
is_flagged_duplicate.description: City's own duplicate flag, parsed from the string 'true'/'false' the API returns.

is_legacy_record.name: is_legacy_record
is_legacy_record.description: True for records migrated from the pre-2018 311 system.

parent_sr_number.name: parent_sr_number
parent_sr_number.description: For a request the City merged into another, the id of the surviving request. NULL otherwise.

ward_raw.name: ward_raw
ward_raw.description: Ward as published, kept as a string so blank and out-of-range values stay countable.

ward.name: ward
ward.description: Ward coerced to an integer in 1-50 by the clean_ward macro, NULL when the raw value is blank or out of range.

community_area.name: community_area
community_area.description: Community area number, 1-77. NULL when the City did not geocode the request.

police_district.name: police_district
police_district.description: Police district the address falls in. Carried as a string because it is zero-padded.

zip_code.name: zip_code
zip_code.description: Five digit ZIP of the service address.

street_address.name: street_address
street_address.description: Service address. Some values contain embedded newlines in the source CSV.

latitude.name: latitude
latitude.description: Latitude in WGS84. NULL for requests with no usable address.

longitude.name: longitude
longitude.description: Longitude in WGS84. NULL for requests with no usable address.

source_file.name: source_file
source_file.description: Raw CSV page the row was loaded from. Kept for lineage when a month needs re-pulling.

model.chicago_311.stg_service_requests.raw_code:
{{
    config(
        materialized = 'view'
    )
}}

-- Staging does renames and typing only. No filtering, no deduplication, no
-- business logic. The row count out of here must equal the row count in
-- raw.service_requests, which the singular test
-- tests/assert_staging_preserves_raw_rowcount.sql enforces. Keeping staging
-- lossless means the data-quality counts in docs/DATA_QUALITY.md can be
-- reproduced against this model rather than against a CSV glob.

with source as (

    select * from {{ source('raw', 'service_requests') }}

),

typed as (

    select
        trim(sr_number)                                     as sr_number,
        trim(sr_type)                                       as sr_type,
        trim(sr_short_code)                                  as sr_short_code,
        trim(owner_department)                               as owner_department,
        trim(status)                                         as status_raw,
        trim(origin)                                         as origin,

        try_cast(created_date as timestamp)                  as created_at,
        try_cast(last_modified_date as timestamp)            as last_modified_at,
        try_cast(closed_date as timestamp)                   as closed_at,

        -- The API returns the literal strings 'true' and 'false', not booleans.
        case lower(trim(duplicate))
            when 'true' then true
            when 'false' then false
        end                                                  as is_flagged_duplicate,
        case lower(trim(legacy_record))
            when 'true' then true
            when 'false' then false

test.chicago_311.assert_closed_not_after.name: assert_closed_not_after_last_modified
test.chicago_311.assert_closed_not_after.raw_code:
-- Business rule: a record cannot be closed after the last time it was touched,
-- because closing it IS touching it.
--
-- This is the test that failed on the raw data. The naive version, with no
-- tolerance, returns 7,886 rows out of 690,427. Before weakening the test I
-- checked the magnitude of the violation:
--
--   select min(d), median(d), max(d) from (
--     select (epoch(closed_at) - epoch(last_modified_at)) as d
--     from stg_service_requests where closed_at > last_modified_at)
--
--   min = 1.0, median = 1.0, max = 1.0   (seconds)
--
-- Every single violation is exactly one second, across all nine service types.
-- That is a write-ordering artifact in the City's own system, where the closure
-- timestamp and the modified timestamp are stamped by different statements, not
-- a corrupted record. A one-second skew changes no closure duration that this
-- project reports, since the smallest unit any mart uses is a minute.
--
-- So the rule is kept but given a two-second tolerance, which still catches a
-- genuine ordering break while not firing on the clock artifact. The defect is
-- recorded as defect 5 in docs/DATA_QUALITY.md with its row count, rather than
-- being silently dropped.

select
    sr_number,
    closed_at,
    last_modified_at,
    epoch(closed_at) - epoch(last_modified_at) as seconds_after_last_modified
from {{ ref('int_service_requests') }}
where closed_at is not null
  and last_modified_at is not null
  and epoch(closed_at) - epoch(last_modified_at) > 2

test.chicago_311.assert_mart_volume_matc.name: assert_mart_volume_matches_fact
test.chicago_311.assert_mart_volume_matc.raw_code:
-- Business rule: the ward mart must not lose or invent requests. Its
-- requests_total summed over all rows has to equal the count of ward-attributed
-- requests in the fact model.
--
-- Worth asserting because the mart has a join to stg_wards. An inner join on a
-- ward that was missing from the seed would quietly drop a whole ward's
-- volume, the chart would still render, and the only symptom would be a
-- citywide total that is slightly too low.
--
-- Allows a difference of exactly zero.

with mart_total as (
    select sum(requests_total) as n from {{ ref('mart_ward_service_performance') }}
),
fact_total as (
    select count(*) as n from {{ ref('int_service_requests') }} where ward is not null
)
select
    mart_total.n as mart_rows,
    fact_total.n as fact_rows,
    mart_total.n - fact_total.n as difference
from mart_total
cross join fact_total
where mart_total.n != fact_total.n

test.chicago_311.assert_staging_preserve.name: assert_staging_preserves_raw_rowcount
test.chicago_311.assert_staging_preserve.raw_code:
-- Business rule about the pipeline itself: staging renames and types, it does
-- not filter. If stg_service_requests has fewer rows than raw.service_requests
-- then a cast or a trim is dropping records, and every data-quality count in
-- docs/DATA_QUALITY.md is being measured against an already-thinned table.
--
-- This is the test that makes the data-quality documentation trustworthy. The
-- counts in that file are taken from staging, and they are only honest if
-- staging is lossless.

    select count(*) as n from {{ ref('stg_service_requests') }}
),
raw_rows as (
    select count(*) as n from {{ source('raw', 'service_requests') }}
)
select
    staged.n as staging_rows,
    raw_rows.n as raw_rows,
    staged.n - raw_rows.n as difference
from staged
cross join raw_rows
where staged.n != raw_rows.n

test.chicago_311.assert_ward_within_chic.name: assert_ward_within_chicago_range
test.chicago_311.assert_ward_within_chic.raw_code:
-- Business rule: Chicago has 50 wards, numbered 1 to 50. A ward of 0, 51 or
-- 999 is not a place, and a ward-level mart built on one would show a bar for
-- a district that does not exist.
--
-- The clean_ward macro is what enforces this, by nulling anything outside the
-- range instead of passing it through. This test is the guard on that macro:
-- if someone edits clean_ward and widens the range, this fails.
--
-- Checked in both directions. First, no out-of-range ward survives into the
-- fact model. Second, every non-null ward in the fact model exists in the
-- ward dimension, which the relationships test also covers but which is
-- cheap to assert here against the literal range.

select
    sr_number,
    ward_raw,
    ward,
    'ward outside 1-50' as failure_reason
from {{ ref('int_service_requests') }}
where ward is not null
  and (ward < 1 or ward > 50)

union all

select
    sr_number,
    ward_raw,
    ward,
    'ward not present in ward dimension' as failure_reason
from {{ ref('int_service_requests') }} r
where r.ward is not null
  and not exists (select 1 from {{ ref('stg_wards') }} w where w.ward = r.ward)

model.chicago_311.mart_data_quality.description: One row per documented data defect with its detection rule, its row count, and how the pipeline handles it. Generated from the same list that docs/DATA_QUALITY.md is written from, so the published counts and the pipeline cannot disagree.

defect_id.name: defect_id
defect_id.description: Matches the numbered section in docs/DATA_QUALITY.md.

detection_rule.name: detection_rule
detection_rule.description: The SQL predicate that identifies affected rows, as text.

handling.name: handling
handling.description: What the pipeline does about it and why.

affected_rows.name: affected_rows
affected_rows.description: Rows in stg_service_requests matching the detection rule.

model.chicago_311.mart_data_quality.raw_code:
-- Every defect from docs/DATA_QUALITY.md as a row, so the counts in that doc
-- and the counts on the dashboard come from the same query and cannot drift
-- apart. Also means a reviewer can check the documented numbers without
-- opening a SQL client.
--
-- affected_rows is measured against stg_service_requests, which is lossless,
-- not against the deduplicated intermediate model. Measuring after the fix
-- would report zero for every defect that staging repairs.

{% set defects = [
    ('1', 'Duplicate requests', 'is_flagged_duplicate', 'Excluded from no mart. Kept, because a resident reporting the same pothole twice is still a report. Flagged so any count can be taken with or without them.'),
    ('2', 'Closed in under one minute', 'days_to_close_raw < 1.0/1440 and days_to_close_raw is not null', 'Not a real closure. Surfaced as share_closed_under_1min in two marts rather than deleted, because deleting it would overstate how fast the remaining work is.'),
    ('3', 'Ward missing or out of range', 'ward is null', 'Nulled by the clean_ward macro. Row kept so citywide totals stay correct, excluded from every ward-level mart.'),
    ('4', 'Closed before created', 'closed_at < created_at', 'Would be impossible. None found in this slice. days_to_close refuses to populate if it ever appears.'),
    ('5', 'Closed after last modified', 'closed_at > last_modified_at', 'Fails a naive ordering test. Every instance is exactly one second, so it is a clock artifact. Test carries a one second tolerance, see tests/assert_closed_not_after_last_modified.sql.'),
    ('6', 'Open longer than a year', 'is_stale_open', 'Backlog rather than live work. Counted separately as requests_stale_open.'),
    ('7', 'Completed with no closed timestamp', 'is_closed_without_timestamp', 'Would make the request unmeasurable. None found in this slice.'),
    ('8', 'No geocode', 'has_no_geocode', 'Blocks map views only. No effect on the ward analysis, which uses the ward field.'),
    ('9', 'Missing ZIP code', 'zip_code is null', 'Known gap. The City populates ZIP inconsistently by intake channel. Not used by any mart.'),
    ('10', 'Dangling parent request id', 'parent_sr_number is not null and not exists (select 1 from staged p where p.sr_number = staged.parent_sr_number)', 'The surviving request this one was merged into is not in the extract, because the extract keeps only nine service types and a parent can be any type. An artifact of the extract filter, not a City defect. No mart joins on parent_sr_number.')
] %}

with staged as (
    select
        s.*,
        {# Recompute the derived flags against staging rather than importing
           them from the intermediate model, so this mart measures the data
           before deduplication. #}
        case
            when s.closed_at is not null
                then {{ duration_days('s.created_at', 's.closed_at') }}
        end as days_to_close_raw,
        (s.status_raw in ('Completed', 'Closed') and s.closed_at is null)
            as is_closed_without_timestamp,
        (s.latitude is null or s.longitude is null) as has_no_geocode,
        (
            s.status_raw = 'Open'
            and {{ duration_days('s.created_at', "'" ~ var('window_end') ~ "'::timestamp") }}
                > {{ var('stale_open_days') }}
        ) as is_stale_open
    from {{ ref('stg_service_requests') }} s
),

total as (
    select count(*) as total_rows from staged
),

counts as (
    {% for id, label, condition, handling in defects %}
    select
        '{{ id }}'                                       as defect_id,
        '{{ label }}'                                    as defect,
        '{{ condition | replace("'", "''") }}'           as detection_rule,
        '{{ handling | replace("'", "''") }}'            as handling,
        count(*)                                         as affected_rows
    from staged
    where {{ condition }}
    {% if not loop.last %}union all{% endif %}
    {% endfor %}
)

select
    c.defect_id,
    c.defect,
    c.detection_rule,
    c.handling,
    c.affected_rows,
    t.total_rows,
    c.affected_rows / nullif(t.total_rows, 0)::double as affected_share
from counts c

analysis.chicago_311.variance_decomposit.name: variance_decomposition
analysis.chicago_311.variance_decomposit.raw_code:
-- How much of the variation in how long a request takes is about the ward, and
-- how much is about which service was requested?
--
-- This is the number the README's headline rests on, so it lives here as SQL
-- rather than in a notebook. Run it with:
--   dbt compile -s variance_decomposition
-- then execute the compiled file in target/compiled/... against the DuckDB file.
--
-- Method: one-way R-squared. For each grouping, predict every request's wait
-- with that group's mean and measure how much of the total sum of squares that
-- removes. Measured on log1p(days_to_close) because closure times are heavily
-- right-skewed and an untransformed R-squared would be dominated by the
-- handful of requests that took two years.
--
-- This is descriptive, not causal. Ward and service type are correlated with
-- each other (a ward with more alleys files more fly-dumping complaints), so
-- the two R-squared values do not add up to the joint one.

with base as (

    select
        ward,
        service_type,
        ln(1 + days_to_close) as y
    from {{ ref('int_service_requests') }}
    where ward is not null
      and days_to_close is not null

),

grand as (
    select avg(y) as y_bar, count(*) as n from base
),

sst as (
    select sum(power(b.y - g.y_bar, 2)) as sst
    from base b cross join grand g
),

by_service as (
    select sum(power(b.y - m.y_hat, 2)) as sse
    from base b
    join (select service_type, avg(y) as y_hat from base group by service_type) m
      on m.service_type = b.service_type
),

by_ward as (
    select sum(power(b.y - m.y_hat, 2)) as sse
    from base b
    join (select ward, avg(y) as y_hat from base group by ward) m
      on m.ward = b.ward
),

by_both as (
    select sum(power(b.y - m.y_hat, 2)) as sse
    from base b
    join (select service_type, ward, avg(y) as y_hat from base group by service_type, ward) m
      on m.service_type = b.service_type and m.ward = b.ward
)

select 'service type only' as grouping, 1 - by_service.sse / sst.sst as r_squared, grand.n as observations
from by_service cross join sst cross join grand
union all
select 'ward only', 1 - by_ward.sse / sst.sst, grand.n
from by_ward cross join sst cross join grand
union all
select 'service type and ward', 1 - by_both.sse / sst.sst, grand.n
from by_both cross join sst cross join grand

model.chicago_311.mart_volume_vs_delay.raw_code:
-- The hypothesis test, as a table.
--
-- If wards wait longer because they file more requests, then (a) across wards,
-- volume and median wait should move together, and (b) within a single ward,
-- its heavier months should be its slower months. This mart computes both
-- correlations so the answer in the README is a number someone can re-derive,
-- not an assertion.
--
-- Grain: one row per service type, plus one row with service_type = 'ALL
-- SERVICES' for the citywide figure.

with panel as (

    select * from {{ ref('int_ward_monthly_load') }}
    where median_days_to_close is not null

),

-- Across-ward view: collapse each ward to a single volume and a single median.
by_ward as (

    select
        ward,
        sum(requests_opened)        as requests_total,
        median(median_days_to_close) as median_days_to_close
    from panel
    group by ward

),

all_services as (

    select
        'ALL SERVICES'                                   as service_type,
        (select count(*) from by_ward)                   as n_wards,
        (select {{ safe_corr('requests_total', 'median_days_to_close') }} from by_ward)
                                                         as corr_ward_volume_vs_delay,
        count(*)                                         as n_ward_months,
        -- Within-ward view. load_index is already normalised to each ward's own
        -- average month, so a positive correlation here means a ward genuinely
        -- slows down when its own workload spikes.
        {{ safe_corr('load_index', 'median_days_to_close') }} as corr_monthly_load_vs_delay,
        median(median_days_to_close)                     as median_days_to_close
    from panel

),

per_service_panel as (

    select
        service_type,
        ward,
        created_month,
        count(*)                                        as requests_opened,
        median(days_to_close)                            as median_days_to_close
    from {{ ref('int_service_requests') }}
    where ward is not null and days_to_close is not null
    group by service_type, ward, created_month
    having count(*) >= 10  -- a monthly median off 3 requests is not a signal

),

per_service_load as (

    select
        *,
        requests_opened / nullif(
            avg(requests_opened) over (partition by service_type, ward), 0
        ) as load_index
    from per_service_panel

),

per_service_by_ward as (

    select
        service_type,
        ward,
        sum(requests_opened)            as requests_total,
        median(median_days_to_close)     as median_days_to_close
    from per_service_load
    group by service_type, ward

),

per_service as (

    select
        l.service_type,
        (select count(*) from per_service_by_ward b where b.service_type = l.service_type)
                                                         as n_wards,
        (select {{ safe_corr('b.requests_total', 'b.median_days_to_close') }}
           from per_service_by_ward b where b.service_type = l.service_type)
                                                         as corr_ward_volume_vs_delay,
        count(*)                                         as n_ward_months,
        {{ safe_corr('l.load_index', 'l.median_days_to_close') }} as corr_monthly_load_vs_delay,
        median(l.median_days_to_close)                   as median_days_to_close
    from per_service_load l
    group by l.service_type

),

combined as (

    select service_type, n_wards, corr_ward_volume_vs_delay,
           n_ward_months, corr_monthly_load_vs_delay, median_days_to_close
    from all_services
    union all
    select service_type, n_wards, corr_ward_volume_vs_delay,
           n_ward_months, corr_monthly_load_vs_delay, median_days_to_close
    from per_service

)

select
    *,
    -- A plain-language read of the across-ward correlation, so the dashboard
    -- and the CSV export say the same thing and neither has to re-interpret it.
    case
        when corr_ward_volume_vs_delay is null then 'Not enough data'
        when corr_ward_volume_vs_delay >= 0.4  then 'Volume explains a lot'
        when corr_ward_volume_vs_delay >= 0.2  then 'Volume explains some'
        when corr_ward_volume_vs_delay > -0.2  then 'Volume explains nothing'
        else 'Busier wards are faster'
    end as volume_verdict
from combined

model.chicago_311.mart_service_type_summ.raw_code:
-- Citywide picture per service type, plus how unequal that service is across
-- wards. This is the table that answers "is the wait about the ward or about
-- the service", because it puts the service-to-service range and the
-- ward-to-ward range side by side in the same units.

with per_ward as (

    select
        service_type,
        ward,
        requests_total,
        requests_measurable,
        median_days_to_close
    from {{ ref('mart_ward_service_performance') }}
    -- Wards with very few closed requests of a type produce unstable medians,
    -- and two of them were enough to make the ward spread look 95x. Floor at
    -- 200 so the inequity numbers reported in the README are about routing and
    -- not about sample size.
    where requests_measurable >= 200

),

citywide as (

    select
        service_type,
        department,
        count(*)                                            as requests_total,
        count(days_to_close)                                as requests_measurable,
        sum(case when is_open then 1 else 0 end)            as requests_open,
        sum(case when is_stale_open then 1 else 0 end)       as requests_stale_open,
        count(days_to_close) / nullif(count(*), 0)::double   as closure_rate,
        median(days_to_close)                                as median_days_to_close,
        avg(days_to_close)                                   as mean_days_to_close,
        quantile_cont(days_to_close, 0.90)                   as p90_days_to_close,
        sum(case when days_to_close < 1.0/1440 then 1 else 0 end)
            / nullif(count(days_to_close), 0)::double        as share_closed_under_1min
    from {{ ref('int_service_requests') }}
    group by service_type, department

),

spread as (

    select
        service_type,
        count(*)                                        as wards_reported,
        quantile_cont(median_days_to_close, 0.10)        as ward_p10_median_days,
        quantile_cont(median_days_to_close, 0.90)        as ward_p90_median_days,
        min(median_days_to_close)                        as ward_fastest_median_days,
        max(median_days_to_close)                        as ward_slowest_median_days,
        -- p90/p10 rather than max/min, because max/min is one ward away
        -- from being noise.
        quantile_cont(median_days_to_close, 0.90)
            / nullif(quantile_cont(median_days_to_close, 0.10), 0) as ward_inequity_ratio,
        {{ safe_corr('requests_total', 'median_days_to_close') }} as corr_volume_vs_delay
    from per_ward
    group by service_type

),

slowest as (

    select service_type, ward, median_days_to_close
    from per_ward
    qualify row_number() over (partition by service_type order by median_days_to_close desc) = 1

),

fastest as (

    select service_type, ward, median_days_to_close
    from per_ward
    qualify row_number() over (partition by service_type order by median_days_to_close asc) = 1

)

select
    c.service_type,
    c.department,
    c.requests_total,
    c.requests_measurable,
    c.requests_open,
    c.requests_stale_open,
    c.closure_rate,
    c.median_days_to_close,
    c.mean_days_to_close,
    c.p90_days_to_close,
    c.share_closed_under_1min,
    coalesce(s.wards_reported, 0)                       as wards_reported,
    s.ward_p10_median_days,
    s.ward_p90_median_days,
    s.ward_fastest_median_days,
    s.ward_slowest_median_days,
    s.ward_inequity_ratio,

    -- Sign and size of this is the whole volume hypothesis, per service type.
    -- Positive means busier wards wait longer, which is the queueing story.
    -- Negative means busier wards are served faster, which is the opposite.
    s.corr_volume_vs_delay,

    sl.ward                                             as slowest_ward,
    sl.median_days_to_close                             as slowest_ward_median_days,
    fa.ward                                             as fastest_ward,
    fa.median_days_to_close                             as fastest_ward_median_days

from citywide c
left join spread s   on s.service_type = c.service_type
left join slowest sl on sl.service_type = c.service_type
left join fastest fa on fa.service_type = c.service_type

### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models
in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the
models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view
shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown
in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`
button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build,
or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.
